t: #3609 Minimum Moves to Reach Target in Grid — Backward Euclid-style Search
o: From (x,y) you may add m = max(x,y) to either coordinate. Forward search explodes, but backwards each point has very few predecessors: if the new x came from adding m to an old max-x, the old point is (X/2, Y) (when X even and X/2 ≥ Y); if it came from adding Y (old x was smaller), it is (X−Y, Y) (valid when X−Y ≤ Y). Symmetrically for y. Example 1 unwinds (5,4)→(1,4)→(1,2) in 2 moves; Example 3 (2,2)→{(0,2),(2,0)} never hits (1,1) → −1. Zeros need care: from (0,0) nothing ever changes.
k: Work backwards: predecessors of (X,Y) are (X−Y, Y) if 0 ≤ X−Y ≤ Y, and (X/2, Y) if X is even and X/2 ≥ Y — plus the mirrored pair.
Jump many subtraction steps at once when chasing a fixed target coordinate (Euclid-style), keeping the recursion logarithmic.
Handle degenerate axes: (0,0) is a fixed point; on an axis only halving applies.

a.i: Recursively unwind the target toward the source. Branching only occurs at ties (X == Y) or halving opportunities, and subtraction chains behave like the Euclidean algorithm, so the explored state count is tiny even for coordinates up to 1e9.
s: If start is (0,0), answer is 0 iff target equals start (nothing can move).
go(X,Y): return 0 on match, infinity if overshoot below the source.
If X > Y: try go(X−Y, Y) (valid when X−Y ≤ Y; jump directly to the source-aligned remainder when chasing) and go(X/2, Y) when X even and X/2 ≥ Y; mirror for Y > X.
If X == Y: try go(0, Y) and go(X, 0). Take the minimum + 1; infinity ⇒ −1.
a.t: O(log²(max coordinate)) amortized — each branch shrinks values Euclid-fast, with memoization on ties/halves.
a.sp: O(number of visited states), small in practice.

w: The crucial insight is inverting the operation: forward BFS is hopeless at 1e9, but each point backwards has at most ~3 predecessors. Pitfalls: mishandling zero coordinates ((0,0) is absorbing; on an axis only halving moves apply), and forgetting that the subtracted amount is the OLD max, which restricts which predecessors are legal. Follow-up: count the number of distinct minimal paths, or ask for reachability only.
